legend: Deep in Busy Beaver's robotics lab sits an experimental Busy Beaver machine. Given a positive integer X%%ZSMJ0%% written in base B%%ZSMJ1%%, it attempts to produce two positive integers Y%%ZSMJ2%% and Z%%ZSMJ3%% such that X+Y=Z%%ZSMJ4%%, and the base-B%%ZSMJ5%% representations of Y%%ZSMJ6%% and Z%%ZSMJ7%% contain exactly the same multiset of digits.

The machine never produces leading zeroes and never outputs numbers with 2⋅105%%ZSMJ8%% or more digits. It has recently stopped functioning, so your task is to determine whether such Y%%ZSMJ9%% and Z%%ZSMJ10%% exist, and to output them if they do. You are given the digits of X%%ZSMJ11%% in base B%%ZSMJ12%% without leading zeroes.
input: The first line contains a single integer T%%ZSMJ13%% (1≤T≤100%%ZSMJ14%%), the number of test cases.
Each test case consists of two lines. The first line of each test case contains two integers N%%ZSMJ15%% and B%%ZSMJ16%% (1≤N≤105%%ZSMJ17%%; 2≤B≤105%%ZSMJ18%%).

The second line of each test case contains N%%ZSMJ19%% integers a1,a2,…,aN%%ZSMJ20%% (0≤ai≤B−1%%ZSMJ21%%; a1≠0%%ZSMJ22%%), representing the digits of X%%ZSMJ23%% in base B%%ZSMJ24%%: X=a1BN−1+a2BN−2+⋯+aN.%%ZSMJ25%%
The sum of N%%ZSMJ26%% over all test cases does not exceed 2⋅105%%ZSMJ27%%.
output: For each test case, if no valid solution exists, output a single line containing NO.
Otherwise, output YES on the first line. On the second line output an integer M%%ZSMJ28%% (1≤M≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ29%%), the number of digits in both Y%%ZSMJ30%% and Z%%ZSMJ31%%.

On the next line output M%%ZSMJ32%% digits p1,p2,…,pM%%ZSMJ33%% (0≤pi≤B−1%%ZSMJ34%%; p1≠0%%ZSMJ35%%), representing Y=p1BM−1+p2BM−2+⋯+pM.%%ZSMJ36%% On the following line output M%%ZSMJ37%% digits q1,q2,…,qM%%ZSMJ38%% (0≤qi≤B−1%%ZSMJ39%%; q1≠0%%ZSMJ40%%), representing Z=q1BM−1+q2BM−2+⋯+qM.%%ZSMJ41%% The digit sequences (p1,…,pM)%%ZSMJ42%% and (q1,…,qM)%%ZSMJ43%% must use exactly the same multiset of digits, and the integers they represent must satisfy X+Y=Z%%ZSMJ44%%. You may print YES and NO in any mixture of uppercase and lowercase letters.
note: In the first test case, with B=10%%ZSMJ45%% and X=36%%ZSMJ46%%, a valid solution is Y=15%%ZSMJ47%% and Z=51%%ZSMJ48%%, since 51=36+15%%ZSMJ49%% and both numbers use the digits {1,5}%%ZSMJ50%%.

In the second test case, with B=5%%ZSMJ51%% and X%%ZSMJ52%% given by digits (1,4,3,4)5%%ZSMJ53%%, X=1⋅53+4⋅52+3⋅51+4=244.%%ZSMJ54%% One valid pair is Y=(1,4,3,2)5=242,Z=(3,4,2,1)5=486,%%ZSMJ55%% which share the digit multiset {1,2,3,4}%%ZSMJ56%% and satisfy X+Y=Z%%ZSMJ57%%.
